subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics Standard 2, Year 12
about: HSC, Models, finance, trigonometry, networks and statistics
syllabus: NSW Mathematics Standard 11-12 Syllabus (2024), Year 12 Standard 2 focus areas

points.title: Simultaneous linear equations
points.brief: Finding where two straight lines meet, by graphing or substitution, and what the point means, such as when two phone plans cost the same.

points.title: Break-even analysis
points.brief: Cost and revenue as straight lines. The business breaks even where they meet, and makes a profit beyond that point.

points.title: Exponential models
points.brief: Growth or decay by a fixed percentage each period, y = a(b)ˣ, as with populations or the value of a car.

points.title: Quadratic models
points.brief: Parabolas that model situations such as the path of a thrown ball or profit against price, and reading the maximum or minimum from the graph.

points.title: Inverse variation models
points.brief: When y = k/x, doubling x halves y, as with travel time and speed for a fixed distance. The graph is a hyperbola.

points.title: The compound interest formula
points.brief: FV = PV(1 + r)ⁿ, adjusting r and n when interest compounds monthly or quarterly.

points.title: Comparing investments
points.brief: Comparing simple and compound interest, and different compounding periods, to choose the better investment.

points.title: Shares and dividends
points.brief: A dividend is a share of a company's profit paid to shareholders. Dividend yield is the yearly dividend as a percentage of the share price.

points.title: Inflation and appreciation
points.brief: Using the compound interest formula to see how prices rise with inflation or how an asset gains value over time.

points.title: Declining balance depreciation
points.brief: An asset loses a fixed percentage of its value each year, S = V₀(1 - r)ⁿ.

points.title: Credit cards
points.brief: Credit card interest is charged daily on the amount owed, often at a high rate, after any interest-free period ends.

points.title: What an annuity is
points.brief: A series of equal payments made at regular intervals that earn compound interest, such as regular saving into an account.

points.title: Future value of an annuity
points.brief: The total an annuity grows to, found from a table of future value interest factors or a spreadsheet.

points.title: Present value from tables
points.brief: The single amount that, invested now, would give the same total as the annuity, found from a table of present value factors.

points.title: Loan repayments
points.brief: A loan is the present value of its repayments, so the table of present value factors gives the repayment for a given loan, rate and term.

points.title: Total interest on a loan
points.brief: The total paid over a loan minus the amount borrowed. Longer terms mean smaller repayments but much more interest.

points.title: Trigonometric ratios in right triangles
points.brief: Using sine, cosine and tangent to find a missing side or angle in a right-angled triangle.

points.title: Elevation and depression
points.brief: The angle of elevation looks up from the horizontal, and the angle of depression looks down. Both are used to find heights and distances.

points.title: True and compass bearings
points.brief: True bearings are three-figure angles clockwise from north, such as 135°T. Compass bearings name an angle from north or south towards east or west, such as S45°E.

points.title: The sine rule in non-right triangles
points.brief: Using a/sin A = b/sin B to find a side or angle when a side and its opposite angle are known.

points.title: The cosine rule in non-right triangles
points.brief: Using c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C to find a side from two sides and the angle between them, or an angle from three sides.

points.title: Area with sine
points.brief: Area = ½ab sin C for a triangle where two sides and the angle between them are known.

points.title: Ratios
points.brief: Simplifying ratios and dividing a quantity in a given ratio, such as sharing $600 in the ratio 2 to 3.

points.title: Scale drawings and plans
points.brief: Using a scale such as 1 to 100 to find real lengths and areas from a plan, and remembering that areas scale by the square.

points.title: Rates and conversions
points.brief: A rate compares two different units, such as km/h or $/kg. Converting a rate, such as km/h to m/s.

points.title: Energy and power
points.brief: Energy used is power times time. Appliances are rated in watts and electricity is billed in kilowatt-hours.

points.title: Speed, distance and time
points.brief: Using speed = distance ÷ time and reading distance-time graphs, where the gradient is the speed.

points.title: Fuel consumption
points.brief: Car fuel use given in litres per 100 km, and working out the fuel and cost of a trip.

points.title: Flow networks
points.brief: A directed network with a source and a sink, where each edge has a capacity, such as cars a road can carry in an hour.

points.title: Cuts
points.brief: A cut separates the source from the sink. Its capacity is the total of the edges that flow from the source side to the sink side.

points.title: Maximum flow and minimum cut
points.brief: The maximum flow through a network equals the capacity of its smallest cut.

points.title: Flow in practice
points.brief: Using maximum flow to find bottlenecks in roads, pipes or data networks, and how raising one edge's capacity may change the flow.

points.title: Activity networks
points.brief: A project drawn as a network, with activities as edges and their durations, and some activities that must wait for others to finish.

points.title: Earliest starting times
points.brief: A forward scan through the network, taking the largest total at each vertex, gives the earliest each activity can start and the project's shortest time.

points.title: Latest starting times
points.brief: A backward scan, taking the smallest value at each vertex, gives the latest each activity can start without delaying the project.

points.title: Float time
points.brief: Float is how long an activity can be delayed without delaying the whole project, the latest start minus the earliest start.

points.title: The critical path
points.brief: The longest path through the network, made of activities with zero float. Any delay on it delays the whole project.

points.title: Scatterplots
points.brief: Plotting pairs of numerical data to see whether two variables are related, with the explanatory variable on the x-axis.

points.title: Correlation
points.brief: Describing a relationship by its direction (positive or negative), form (linear or not) and strength (strong, moderate or weak).

points.title: Pearson's correlation coefficient
points.brief: r runs from -1 to 1 and measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship. It is found with a calculator.

points.title: Least-squares regression line
points.brief: The line of best fit found by a calculator, used to predict one variable from the other.

points.title: Interpolation and extrapolation
points.brief: Predicting inside the range of the data is interpolation and fairly reliable. Predicting outside it is extrapolation and less reliable.

points.title: Correlation and causation
points.brief: Two variables can move together without one causing the other, often because of a third factor.

points.title: Relative frequency
points.brief: The number of times an event happened divided by the number of trials, used to estimate probability. More trials give a better estimate.

points.title: Expected frequency
points.brief: The probability of an event times the number of trials, the number of times it is expected to happen.

points.title: Two-way tables
points.brief: Tables that sort data by two categories, used to find probabilities and compare groups.

points.title: Multistage events
points.brief: Tree diagrams and tables for events with two or more steps, multiplying along branches.

points.title: Complementary events
points.brief: The probability something does not happen is 1 minus the probability it does.

points.title: Features of a normal distribution
points.brief: A bell-shaped, symmetric distribution in which the mean, median and mode are equal.

points.title: Standardised scores
points.brief: z = (x - mean) ÷ standard deviation, the number of standard deviations a score is from the mean.

points.title: The empirical rule
points.brief: The 68, 95, 99.7 rule. In a normal distribution, about 68% of scores lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean, 95% within 2 and 99.7% within 3.

points.title: Comparing scores with z-scores
points.brief: Converting scores from different tests to z-scores to see which performance was better relative to its group.

points.title: Quality control
points.brief: Using the normal distribution to decide whether a product, such as a bottle's fill, is within an acceptable range.
